facts.statement: Sulcavis lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The genus Sulcavis was described by O'Connor and colleagues in 2013.
facts.quote: authority: O'Connor et al., 2013

facts.statement: Sulcavis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean birds.
facts.quote: Sulcavis is a genus of enantiornithean birds.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sulcavis were found in rocks dated between 121 and 125 million years ago in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The fossil was found in Early Cretaceous (121-125 million years ago) rocks in Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: Sulcavis is the first bird species discovered to have ornamented tooth enamel.
facts.quote: Sulcavis is the first discovery of a bird with ornamented tooth enamel.

facts.statement: Sulcavis possessed robust teeth with internal grooves that likely helped them withstand harder food items.
facts.quote: Sulcavis had robust teeth with grooves on the inside surface, which likely strengthened the teeth against harder food items.

facts.statement: The holotype of Sulcavis was discovered near the town of Lamadong in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The holotype of Sulcavis, BMNH Ph-000805, is discovered near the town of Lamadong, in Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: The Sulcavis fossil was found in the Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: The fossil was found in the Yixian Formation, an Early Cretaceous rock formation.

facts.statement: The genus Sulcavis was formally described on January 9, 2013, by a team including Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor and others.
facts.quote: The genus was described on January 9, 2013, in an article that was published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology by Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Yuguang Zhang, Luis Maria Chiappe, Qingjin Meng, Li Quanguo and Liu Di.

facts.statement: The genus name Sulcavis combines the Latin words for 'groove' and 'bird' to reflect its unique dental features.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from the Latin words "sulcus" (groove) and "avis" (bird), reflecting the unusual dental characteristics of the genus.

facts.statement: The species name 'geeorum' honors the Gee family for their contributions to Mesozoic bird research.
facts.quote: The specific name is to honour the Gee family from La Cañada (US) "because of their generous contributions to the research of Mesozoic birds".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Sulcavis geeorum was prepared by Maureen Walsh at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.
facts.quote: The holotype of Sulcavis geeorum was prepared by Maureen Walsh at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, USA.

facts.statement: Sulcavis belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: subclassis: Enantiornithes

facts.statement: Sulcavis is a monotypic extinct genus of Enantiornithes birds that lived in what is now China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Sulcavis es un género monotípico extinto de aves del grupo Enantiornithes que vivió en lo que ahora es China durante el Cretácico temprano.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Sulcavis appeared in the Jehol Biota within the Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles aparecieron en la biota de Jehol, en la Formación de Yixian.

facts.statement: The genus name Sulcavis refers to the grooves on its teeth, which make it unique.
facts.quote: El nombre del género "Sulcavis" proviene del latín "sulcus" (ranura, surco) y "avis" (ave), en referencia a las acanaladuras de sus dientes, que le hacen único.

facts.statement: Sulcavis differs from other Enantiornithes by having enlarged teeth with grooves on their inner surface.
facts.quote: Se diferencia de otros Enantiornithes por sus dientes, que están agrandados y presentan ranuras en su superficie lingual.

facts.statement: The closest relative to Sulcavis is the genus Shenqiornis.
facts.quote: El género más cercano es Shenqiornis.

facts.statement: Sulcavis is part of the parent group Bohaiornithidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Bohaiornithidae

facts.statement: The time range for Sulcavis is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
